notes: One engine-assisted reviewer compared paired and separately searched Stockfish lines before viewing classifier outputs.

cases.rationale: Kg8 is the paired leading choice. Later e-pawn activity does not establish a mistake at this move.
Both engine choices lose and permit the same b-pawn to promote. The sequences differ in whether a queen exchange happens first, with no separate strategic concession established.
Rxb6 is the paired leading choice and still allows h8=Q. The later conversion is not evidence of an earlier error.
Kh2 is the engine's leading choice. The race leaves the d-pawn able to promote in both supplied searches.
Na7 and Nc7 have similar scores and both can restrain the a-pawn. The promotion recorded later does not distinguish these choices.
After Kh6, Rf8 and Kxg7 leave the b8 rook available to Rxb8. The g-pawn is taken in both engine variations and does not account for the immediate rook loss.
Both king or a-pawn choices are already lost to the same g-pawn. The two searches give the same mate distance after the compared moves.
f3 is the leading choice. The engine lets the b-pawn promote anyway, while advancing Black's own counterplay.
Rb2 exchanges the rook for the promoted piece via Rxb8. Bg5 instead leaves the new queen on the board during Black's checks and yields a corroborated mating evaluation.
g8=Q is the leading choice. The c-pawn promotes in both searches and White keeps the better prospects in the queen ending.
Nxg4 changes the immediate captures but still loses to the same h-pawn. The alternatives give comparable already-lost mating outcomes.
Bb2 is the leading choice. The underpromotion and exchange on c1 occur anyway and do not establish an error at Bb2.
Kc4 and Kc5 have similar paired and separately searched scores. The g-pawn remains a threat whichever king move is used.
Rc5+ is the leading choice. The b-pawn can promote in it, so the recorded promotion is not evidence that Rc5+ was inferior.
Rxb7 is the leading choice and both searches show c8=Q followed by the queen liquidation. There is no inferior played choice to diagnose.
The played check shares the leading draw score. The advanced pawn does not distinguish a losing alternative within this decision.
Rd3 is the leading choice and gives Black repeated rook checks while the c-pawn remains blocked.
The paired comparison favours b4 modestly, while the independent replies defend against g3 similarly. The d-pawn persists and no specific promotion consequence is established.
Nf4 is the leading choice. The different early tactical lines arise after that same move.
Nf3 is the leading choice and keeps the material and evaluation advantage. There is no measured played-move error here.
Nbd2 allows Ne2+ and Qxg4+, losing the queen in both inferior variations. The advanced e-pawn helps the attack without promoting.
Qe1 is the leading choice. Both searches show the g3 pawn being removed after the forcing exchanges.
Kg1 is the leading choice in an already lost position. Re2 and the central pawn activity do not by themselves identify a mistake by White.
Rc6 is the leading choice. Both continuations show Black's king reaching the g-pawn and taking it.
Nf3 is the leading choice. Black's own d-pawn advances later and White does not gain a promotion from the decision.
Black is already lost to the connected passers. The paired frame changes which white pawn promotes, while the independent scores do not confirm a worse result after Ng8.
dxc5 is the leading choice. Later white d-pawn activity does not identify a mistake on this move.
Rxb6 is the paired leading choice and removes the advanced pawn before the subsequent central play.
Re6 is the leading choice and both searches show the c3 pawn taken amid the knight exchanges.
Rxd1 is the leading choice and both searches keep the c7 pawn from promotion in the displayed window.
